rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient at mid temperature to elute all 8 compounds if possible and reveal the overall elution window. This should minimize truncation risk while giving useful first-pass information on retention spread and any severe co-elutions.

The only serious problem is the tight 4/5 pair near 7.4 min, while all compounds already elute before 10 min. Doubling tG tests whether that pair is slope-responsive and should spread under a shallower gradient without risking truncation.

The bad pair is clearly slope-responsive: at tG 40 all pairs are resolved, but the run is too long. Try an intermediate gradient time to find the shortest fully resolved method while keeping the same broad window and temperature.

The optimum tG should lie between 20 and 30 min, and 30 min introduced a new late critical pair while 20 min was faster but left only one bad pair. Testing 24 min refines the slope near the likely time-optimal region for full or near-full resolution.

The 4/5 pair is strongly slope-responsive but still unresolved at practical tG, so temperature is the next lever for selectivity. Lowering T may reorder or separate that close pair while preserving the favorable short run seen at tG 20.

At 25 C the critical pair is nearly resolved and the time penalty is still small, so a modest increase in tG is the most likely way to push the remaining pair above R = 1.5. This targets the shortest fully resolved method near the current best conditions.

We now know 22 min at 25 C fully resolves everything but is slower than the near-optimal 20 min run. Raising temperature slightly from 25 to 30 C at tG 20 may keep the improved selectivity while pulling t_last closer to 10 min and improving CRF.

25 C improved the critical selectivity relative to 40 C, while 30 C shifted the weak pair earlier; testing 35 C helps map the temperature-dependent reordering behavior around the current best short method. Lowering phi1 to 0.90 fixed the weak pair, so narrowing the gradient window one more step may preserve full resolution while improving selectivity more efficiently than increasing tG. Injection 12 is fully resolved and very close to the 10 min target, so the best chance to improve CRF is to shorten the gradient one step. This tests whether full resolution is retained with a smaller time penalty.

Since the boundary failure remains the same 3/4 pair when tG is shortened, try shifting the window slightly higher in phi instead of changing slope. Raising phi0 one more step may reduce t_last further while preserving enough selectivity to keep the critical pair resolved.

The successful method appears near the edge of losing the 3/4 pair as phi0 rises, so try narrowing the window slightly from the top while keeping phi0 at the proven optimum. This may preserve full resolution and still shorten the active gradient enough to keep CRF at 1.000.
